title: 42 Pa.C.S. § 5523 — Four year limitation
content:
42 Pa.C.S. § 5523

§ 5523. Four year limitation.

The following actions and proceedings must be commenced within four years:

(1) An action upon a judgment or decree of any court of the United States or of any state.

(2) An action upon a contract, under seal or otherwise, for the rent of any lands, tenements or hereditaments or for the sale of any goods, wares or merchandise.

(7) An action for injury to the person or for the injuries for which relief is provided in 42 Pa.C.S. § 8340.2 (relating to damages in tort actions).

title: Fisher v. Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission, 464 A.2d 659 (Pa. 1983)
content:
Fisher v. Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission, 464 A.2d 659 (Pa. 1983).

[Excerpt — holding summary.]

The Supreme Court of Pennsylvania held that an administrative agency's interpretation of its governing statute is entitled to deference when the statute is ambiguous and the agency's construction is reasonable.

opinionParts.content: An administrative agency's reasonable interpretation of an ambiguous statute is entitled to deference.

title: 42 Pa.C.S. § 8340.2 — Comparative negligence
content:
42 Pa.C.S. § 8340.2

§ 8340.2. Comparative negligence.

(a) General rule.--In all actions brought to recover damages for negligence resulting in death or injury to person or property, the fact that the plaintiff may have been guilty of contributory negligence shall not bar a recovery by the plaintiff or his legal representative, if such negligence was not greater than the causal negligence of the defendant or defendants against whom recovery is sought.

title: N.J. Stat. Ann. § 2A:14-1 — Limitations of actions
content:
N.J. Stat. Ann. § 2A:14-1

2A:14-1. Actions for injury to person or property; actions for taking or injuring personal property.

Every action at law for an injury to the person or for injury to personal property caused by the wrongful act, neglect or default of any person within this State, and every action at law for taking, detaining or injuring personal property shall be commenced within 6 years next after the cause of any such action shall have accrued.

title: Higgs v. Manzi, 88 N.J. 346 (1982)
content:
Higgs v. Manzi, 88 N.J. 346 (1982).

[Excerpt — holding summary.]

The Supreme Court of New Jersey held that a social guest may recover for injuries caused by a host's negligent failure to maintain safe premises, applying ordinary negligence principles to social host-guest relationships.

opinionParts.content: A social guest may recover for injuries caused by a host's negligent failure to maintain safe premises.

title: N.J. Stat. Ann. § 34:15-7 — Workers' compensation exclusive remedy
content:
N.J. Stat. Ann. § 34:15-7

34:15-7. Compensation for injury or death; exclusive remedy.

If an employee receives a personal injury from accident arising out of and in the course of his employment, of which the actual or lawfully imputed negligence of the employer or any other employee is the natural and proximate cause, he shall receive compensation therefor from his employer as provided in this chapter.

title: N.Y. CPLR 214 — Actions to recover damages for personal injury
content:
N.Y. CPLR 214

§ 214. Actions to recover damages for personal injury.

The following actions shall be commenced within three years:

1. an action to recover damages for a personal injury;

2. an action to recover damages for an injury to property.

title: McDougall v. Black & Decker (U.S.A.), Inc., 73 N.Y.2d 955 (1989)
court: Court of Appeals of New York
content:
McDougall v. Black & Decker (U.S.A.), Inc., 73 N.Y.2d 955 (1989).

[Excerpt — holding summary.]

The Court of Appeals held that a manufacturer may be held strictly liable for a defective product that causes injury when the product is used in a reasonably foreseeable manner, even if the user deviates from intended use in a foreseeable way.

opinionParts.content: Strict liability applies when a defective product causes injury in a reasonably foreseeable manner of use.

title: N.Y. Lab. Law § 240 — Scaffolding and safety devices
content:
N.Y. Lab. Law § 240

§ 240. Scaffolding and other devices for use of employees.

1. All scaffolding and other devices mentioned in this section placed or operated as provided in this section shall be so constructed, placed and operated as to give proper protection to a person so employed.

2. A person employing or directing another to perform labor of any kind in the erection, repairing, altering, painting, cleaning or pointing of a building or structure shall furnish or erect, or cause to be furnished or erected for the performance of such labor, scaffolding, hoists, stays, ladders, slings, hangers, blocks, pulleys, braces, irons, ropes, and other devices which shall be so constructed, placed and operated as to give proper protection to a person so employed.

title: Cal. Civ. Code § 335.1 — Limitations on actions for injury to person
content:
Cal. Civ. Code § 335.1

335.1. Within two years: An action for assault, battery, or injury to, or for the death of, an individual caused by the wrongful act or neglect of another.

title: Li v. Yellow Cab Co., 13 Cal. 3d 804 (1975)
content:
Li v. Yellow Cab Co., 13 Cal. 3d 804 (1975).

[Excerpt — holding summary.]

The Supreme Court of California abolished the contributory negligence doctrine and adopted pure comparative negligence, holding that a plaintiff's recovery is reduced in proportion to the plaintiff's fault but is not barred entirely.

opinionParts.content: California adopted pure comparative negligence; a plaintiff's recovery is reduced in proportion to fault but not barred entirely.

title: Cal. Civ. Code § 1714 — Liability for torts
content:
Cal. Civ. Code § 1714

1714. (a) Everyone is responsible, not only for the result of his or her willful acts, but also for an injury occasioned to another by his or her want of ordinary care or skill in the management of his or her property or person, except so far as the latter has, willfully or by want of ordinary care, brought the injury upon himself or herself.

title: Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code § 16.003 — Personal injury
content:
Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code § 16.003

Sec. 16.003. PERSONAL INJURY. (a) A person must bring suit for trespass for injury to the estate or to the property of another, conversion of personal property, taking or detaining the personal property of another, personal injury, forcible entry and detainer, and forcible detainer not later than two years after the day the cause of action accrues.

title: Hyland v. Ray Bros. & Co., 953 S.W.2d 840 (Tex. App. 1997)
court: Court of Appeals of Texas, San Antonio
content:
Hyland v. Ray Bros. & Co., 953 S.W.2d 840 (Tex. App. 1997).

[Excerpt — holding summary.]

The court addressed contract interpretation and held that when contract terms are unambiguous, the court must enforce the contract as written without adding terms or rewriting the parties' agreement.

opinionParts.content: When contract terms are unambiguous, courts must enforce the contract as written without rewriting the parties' agreement.

title: Tex. Bus. & Com. Code § 2.314 — Implied warranty: merchantability
content:
Tex. Bus. & Com. Code § 2.314

Sec. 2.314. IMPLIED WARRANTY: MERCHANTABILITY; USAGE OF TRADE. (a) Unless excluded or modified, a warranty that the goods shall be merchantable is implied in a contract for their sale if the seller is a merchant with respect to goods of that kind.

title: Fla. Stat. § 95.11 — Limitations other than for recovery of real property
content:
Fla. Stat. § 95.11

95.11 Limitations other than for the recovery of real property.—Actions other than for recovery of real property shall be commenced as follows:

(3) WITHIN FOUR YEARS.—
(a) An action relating to the design, planning, or construction of an improvement to real property.

(4) WITHIN FIVE YEARS.—
(b) A legal or equitable action on a contract, obligation, or liability not founded on a written instrument.

title: Rhr Int'l, Ltd. v. U.S. Trust Co. of Florida, 919 So. 2d 332 (Fla. 2006)
content:
Rhr Int'l, Ltd. v. U.S. Trust Co. of Florida, 919 So. 2d 332 (Fla. 2006).

[Excerpt — holding summary.]

The Supreme Court of Florida addressed contract interpretation and held that ambiguous contract terms are construed against the drafter when the drafter caused the ambiguity.

opinionParts.content: Ambiguous contract terms are construed against the drafter when the drafter caused the ambiguity.

title: Fla. Stat. § 768.81 — Comparative fault
content:
Fla. Stat. § 768.81

768.81 Comparative fault.—In a negligence action, contributory fault chargeable to the claimant diminishes proportionately the amount awarded as economic and noneconomic damages for an injury attributable to the claimant's contributory fault, but does not bar recovery.

title: 735 ILCS 5/13-202 — Actions based on personal injuries
content:
735 ILCS 5/13-202

Sec. 13-202. Actions based on personal injuries.

Actions for damages for an injury to the person, other than for injury to the character or reputation, or actions based upon statutory liability for injury to the person, shall be commenced within 2 years next after the cause of action accrued.

title: Murphy v. City of Chicago, 352 Ill. App. 3d 1 (2004)
court: Appellate Court of Illinois, First District
content:
Murphy v. City of Chicago, 352 Ill. App. 3d 1 (2004).

[Excerpt — holding summary.]

The appellate court addressed municipal liability and held that a municipality may be liable for willful and wanton conduct in maintaining public property when it has actual or constructive notice of a dangerous condition.

opinionParts.content: A municipality may be liable for willful and wanton conduct when it has notice of a dangerous condition on public property.

title: 740 ILCS 110/2 — Illinois Human Rights Act purpose
content:
740 ILCS 110/2

Sec. 2. Declaration of Policy. It is the public policy of this State to secure for all individuals within Illinois the freedom from discrimination against any individual because of his or her race, color, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, age, order of protection status, marital status, disability, military status, sexual orientation, pregnancy, or unfavorable discharge from military service in connection with employment, real estate transactions, access to financial credit, and the availability of public accommodations.

title: M.G.L. c. 260, § 2A — Actions of tort for personal injuries
content:
M.G.L. c. 260, § 2A

Section 2A. Actions of tort for personal injuries to the person or for consequential damages shall be commenced only within three years next after the cause of action accrues.

title: Ayres v. R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co., 437 Mass. 504 (2002)
content:
Ayres v. R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co., 437 Mass. 504 (2002).

[Excerpt — holding summary.]

The Supreme Judicial Court addressed consumer protection in tobacco litigation and held that claims under Chapter 93A require a showing that the defendant's conduct was unfair or deceptive within the meaning of the statute.

opinionParts.content: Chapter 93A claims require a showing that the defendant's conduct was unfair or deceptive within the meaning of the statute.

title: M.G.L. c. 93A, § 2 — Unfair or deceptive acts or practices
content:
M.G.L. c. 93A, § 2

Section 2. Unfair methods of competition and unfair or deceptive acts or practices in the conduct of any trade or commerce are hereby declared unlawful.

title: Va. Code § 8.01-243 — Personal actions based on contracts
content:
Va. Code § 8.01-243

§ 8.01-243. Personal actions based on contracts.

Unless otherwise provided by law, actions founded upon a contract, other than actions on a judgment or decree of a court of record of the Commonwealth or of the United States, shall be brought within five years after the cause of action accrues.

title: Commonwealth v. Epps, 287 Va. 436 (2014)
content:
Commonwealth v. Epps, 287 Va. 436 (2014).

[Excerpt — holding summary.]

The Supreme Court of Virginia addressed statutory interpretation and held that courts must apply the plain meaning of unambiguous statutory language unless the result would be absurd.

opinionParts.content: Courts must apply the plain meaning of unambiguous statutory language unless the result would be absurd.

title: Va. Code § 8.01-581.15 — Medical malpractice review
content:
Va. Code § 8.01-581.15

§ 8.01-581.15. Review of medical malpractice by medical malpractice review panel.

In any action for damages for medical malpractice against a health care provider, the plaintiff shall submit the claim to a medical malpractice review panel prior to filing a civil action in any court.

title: 10 Del. C. § 8119 — Limitations of actions for personal injury
content:
10 Del. C. § 8119

§ 8119. Limitations of actions for personal injury.

No action for the recovery of damages upon a liability created by law, or upon a contract, express or implied, for the recovery of a penalty or forfeiture, or for assault, battery, false imprisonment, libel, slander, replevin, malicious prosecution, or for any injury to the person or reputation of another, or for the taking or injuring of any goods or chattels, shall be brought after the expiration of 2 years from the accruing of the cause of such action.

title: Moyer v. Phillips, 397 A.2d 1004 (Del. 1978)
content:
Moyer v. Phillips, 397 A.2d 1004 (Del. 1978).

[Excerpt — holding summary.]

The Supreme Court of Delaware addressed premises liability and held that a landowner owes a duty of reasonable care to invitees to keep the premises in a reasonably safe condition.

opinionParts.content: A landowner owes a duty of reasonable care to invitees to keep the premises in a reasonably safe condition.

title: 6 Del. C. § 18-1104 — Limited liability of members
content:
6 Del. C. § 18-1104

§ 18-1104. Limited liability of members.

Except as otherwise provided in this chapter, the debts, obligations and liabilities of a limited liability company, whether arising in contract, tort or otherwise, shall be solely the debts, obligations and liabilities of the limited liability company, and no member or manager of a limited liability company shall be personally liable for any such debt, obligation or liability of the limited liability company solely by reason of being or acting as a member or manager.
